title: The words jazz and funk
summary: Wooding discusses when he first heard the word jazz and how jazz and funk came to mean what they do.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: When was the first time you recall hearing the term 'jazz' used?
Jazz?
Yeah.

Well, the first time that I ever heard of jazz was after we come back here, let's see -- well, in Atlantic City, we started playing it. Because I opened up with a -- I opened down there and then there were -- Ed Major who was with Charley Johnson -- they played quite a lot of jazz. They played jazz -- it wasn't the livery stable jazz, not Dixieland Jazzband. We had a lot of jazz before that.
But I mean the use of the term, 'jazz'. Was it called, 'jazz'?
Well, it was begin to be called jazz. Because jazz has a funny word -- jazz means nothing.
Right, but what I'm trying to get at is, for instance, that the word 'jazz', before it was applied to music, was it used for other things, did it have another
Well, a lot of people used 'jazz' because they sounded old timey if they said, 'ragtime'. Because that was the next term thing in.
Right. Did they talk about, 'jazzing things up' ?

Absolutely, it meant just playing around, butterflying around, or a bunch of guys together, whooping it up or something like that, and they'd say, "Man, all that jazz." Jazz, it meant nothing. There was nothing going on worth a quarter. But a lot of guys just beating up their gums and things like that, you know what I mean?
And then they got so they applied it to jazz. It's just like the word, 'gutbucket', and 'funk'.
Uh hunh.
Funk, at one time, meant stinking.
I think it still does.

(unintelligible) -- man, the funk was so thick you could cut it with a knife. Meaning, at a house rent party, or something like that, the women and all was dancing running around and screwing around, and you see, everything was all mixed up,

and, you know what I mean? I don't mean that they would do anything sexually. They're screwing around. You know, everybody was just having a good time and so, the guy would come in door and say, "Whew, open the window in here, it smells funky in here." But now, it has a different meaning. Right.

But now, then it got to be a -- and I was wondering about that, because in Germany, funk means, in reference to the radio. Well, I wondered if some people took it and identified that as a -- to make funk, you know what I mean. Cause I, even now, I tell some of the guys now, "Look make that song Sound funky."
Right.
But, that's not it. You know what I mean? So, maybe that's the wrong way to look at it. You see? But that's the way those things started. Like you said, we used to say 'jazz it up'.
Right.
Then, and then, we go -- the first word was, "Get hot, boys."
Um hunh.

The we got to say, "Jazz it." And now they say, "Put some funk in it. Make it, you know what I mean." These are just words, and somebody coined them, and made them step into the English exagerrated and they stuck into the language.
Right.
You see, I think that's where that started.
